drivingQuestion: Which tanna holds that a sukka at the top of a ship is fit, and what exactly divides Rabban Gamliel and R' Akiva?
outcomeNote: The mishna is R' Akiva's; Abaye fixes the scope and basis of the dispute.

segments.he: גְּמָ׳ מַנִּי מַתְנִיתִין — רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא הִיא. דְּתַנְיָא: הָעוֹשֶׂה סוּכָּתוֹ בְּרֹאשׁ הַסְּפִינָה — רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל פּוֹסֵל, וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא מַכְשִׁיר.
segments.en: «GEMARA:» The Gemara comments: In accordance with «whose» opinion is «the mishna?» It «is» in accordance with the opinion of «Rabbi Akiva, as it is taught» in a baraita: In the case of «one who establishes his sukka at the top of the ship, Rabban Gamliel deems» it «unfit and Rabbi Akiva deems» it «fit.»

segments.he: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא שֶׁהָיוּ בָּאִין בִּסְפִינָה, עָמַד רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא וְעָשָׂה סוּכָּה בְּרֹאשׁ הַסְּפִינָה. לְמָחָר נָשְׁבָה רוּחַ וַעֲקָרַתָּה. אָמַר לוֹ רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל: עֲקִיבָא! הֵיכָן סוּכָּתְךָ?
segments.en: There was «an incident involving Rabban Gamliel and Rabbi Akiva, who were coming on a ship. Rabbi Akiva arose and established a sukka at the top of the ship. The next day the wind blew and uprooted it. Rabban Gamliel said to him: Akiva, where is your sukka?» It was unfit from the start.

segments.he: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא, הֵיכָא דְּאֵינָהּ יְכוֹלָה לַעֲמוֹד בְּרוּחַ מְצוּיָה דְּיַבָּשָׁה — לֹא כְּלוּם הִיא. יְכוֹלָה לַעֲמוֹד בְּשֶׁאֵינָהּ מְצוּיָה דְּיַבָּשָׁה, כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי דִּכְשֵׁרָה. כִּי פְּלִיגִי בְּדִיכוֹלָה לַעֲמוֹד בְּרוּחַ מְצוּיָה דְּיַבָּשָׁה וְאֵינָהּ יְכוֹלָה לַעֲמוֹד (בְּרוּחַ שֶׁאֵינָהּ מְצוּיָה דְּיַבָּשָׁה). רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל סָבַר: סוּכָּה דִּירַת קֶבַע בָּעֵינַן, וְכֵיוָן דְּאֵינָהּ יְכוֹלָה לַעֲמוֹד בְּרוּחַ מְצוּיָה דְּיָם — לֹא כְּלוּם הִיא. רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא סָבַר: סוּכָּה דִּירַת עֲרַאי בָּעֵינַן, וְכֵיוָן דִּיכוֹלָה לַעֲמוֹד בְּרוּחַ מְצוּיָה דְּיַבָּשָׁה — כְּשֵׁרָה.
segments.en: «Abaye said: Everyone agrees that» in a case «where» the sukka «is unable to withstand a typical land wind,» the sukka «is of no consequence» and it is not even a temporary residence. If «it is able to withstand» even «an atypical land wind, everyone agrees that» the sukka «is fit. Where they disagree» is «in» a case «where» the sukka «is able to withstand a typical land wind but is unable to withstand an atypical land wind,» which is the equivalent of a typical sea wind. «Rabban Gamliel holds:» In order to fulfill the mitzva of «sukka, we require a permanent residence, and since it is not able to withstand» an atypical land wind, which is like «a typical sea wind, it is of no consequence» and is not a sukka at all. «Rabbi Akiva holds:» In order to fulfill the mitzva of «sukka, we require a temporary residence, and since it is able to withstand a typical land wind,» it «is fit,» although it is unable to withstand a typical sea wind.
